title: Whoever is attached to something will be entrusted to that thing
hadeeth: ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Akīm (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever is attached to something will be entrusted to that thing."
attribution: Narrated by At-Termedhy - Narrated by Ahmad
explanation: Whoever turns with his heart or deeds or both to something hoping that it would benefit him or keep harm away, then Allah will entrust him to that thing that he is attached to. So, whoever is attached to Allah, Allah shall grant him sufficiency and will make every difficult affair easy for him, and whoever is attached to anything other than Allah, then Allah will entrust him to it and it will fail him.
hints: It forbids attachment to other than Allah Almighty.
It is obligatory to be attached to Allah in all one’s affairs.
It highlights the harm of Shirk and its evil consequences.
One is recompensed, good or bad, according to their deeds.
Whoever turns away from Allah and seeks help from others than Him shall be failed.
hadeeth_ar: عن عبد الله بن عكيم رضي الله عنه مرفوعاً: «مَنْ تَعَلَّقَ شيئا وُكِلَ إليه».
explanation_ar: من التفت بقلبه أو فعله أو بهما جميعا إلى شيء يرجو منه النفع أو دفع الضر وكله الله إلى ذلك الشيء الذي تعلَّقه، فمن تعلَّق بالله كفاه ويسَّر له كل عسير، ومن تعلق بغيره وكله الله إلى ذلك الشيء وخذله.
hints_ar: وجوب التعلق بالله في جميع الأمور.
أن نتيجة العمل ترجع إلى العامل خيرا أو شرا.
خذلان من انصرف عن الله وطلب النفع من غيره.

words_meanings_ar.meaning: أي التفت قلبُه إلى شيءٍ يعتقد أنه ينفعه أو يدفع عنه.
أي وكله الله إلى ذلك الشيء الذي تعلَّقَه من دونه وخذله.
